description: Schwarz-Christoffel mappings provide explicit conformal maps from the disk to polygonal domains. Combined with interval arithmetic (as in Tucker's work on Smale's 14th problem), this enables rigorous, computer-verified bounds on the Bloch constant. The SC Toolbox (Driscoll-Trefethen) provides the computational backbone, while interval extensions provide mathematical certainty.
mathematical_formalization: The SC map f(z) = A + C int_0^z prod_{k=1}^n (1 - zeta/z_k)^{alpha_k - 1} dzeta maps D to a polygon P. Using interval arithmetic: [f]([z]) supset { f(z) : z in [z] }, ensuring rigorous enclosures. The Bloch radius B_f = sup{ r : exists Omega subset D, f|_Omega univalent, f(Omega) supset D(w,r) }.
analogical_connections: Interval SC mapping ~ error-bounded finite element analysis
Rigorous enclosure of conformal map ~ formal verification of software
Parameter problem in SC ~ inverse problem in tomography
implementation_hypothesis: Extend the SC Toolbox to use interval arithmetic (INTLAB or Julia IntervalArithmetic.jl). For candidate extremal polygonal domains, compute rigorous enclosures of the conformal map and its derivative. Verify that the computed Bloch radius has guaranteed lower/upper bounds. Start with simple polygons (strips, L-shapes) and progress to more complex candidates.
experiment_seed: Implement SC mapping with interval arithmetic for the infinite strip of width pi (known: inradius = pi/4). Verify the rigorous bound. Then apply to n-gon approximations of the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda domain. Compare interval-verified bounds with floating-point results.
